This is translated by GOPANI (1989:132-3) as follows: 


That very wind, when it is suspended and stopped at the navel 
is called Kumbhaka. The Pratyahara is that type of pranayam in 
which the breath is moved from one part of the body to another. 
When the breath is prevented from escaping through the palate, 
nostrils or mouth, it is called the Shanta. That pranayam in which 
the wind is drawn from outside and stored in the region of the 
heart is called the Uttara. When it is shifted to the lower parts of 
the body, such as the navel etc., it is named the Adhara. 


The difference here between kumbhaka and Santa seems to lie only in 
the place within the body where the breath is retained.

the nostril of the left [side of the] nose’

whether praganta is the fourth stage of each cycle of pranayama or a

not clear whether the breath is to be released in this way after prasanta 
or after kumbhaka.

A NOTE ON THE APPENDICES 


In the pages that follow, the reader will find extracts relevant to the con- 
stitution and interpretation of the first three sütras of the Nisvasa that are 
too long to be included in the notes. It is to be noted that these portions 
have been only minimally edited. 

In the case of the Svacchanda, portions of chapters 7, 11 and 12 have been 
included that are plainly based on the Nayasutra. We could simply have re- 
ferred readers to the KSTS edition, but for these passages the text of the 
Svacchanda that is reflected in old Nepalese manuscripts is clearly often clos- 
er to that of the Nayasütra than is the polished up Kashmirian text on which 
Ksemaraja commented. As SANDERSON has shown (2005:243), the trans- 
mission of the Netratantra is similar to that of the Svacchanda: there too 
the printed Kashmirian version differs from what the Nepalese manuscripts 
transmit, notably in that it is grammatically more correct. 


With the exception of an insertion of 95 verses seen in the Nepalese 
manuscript the only major difference between the transmissions of the 
Netratantra in that and the Kashmirian manuscripts is that the devia- 
tions from strictly grammatical Sanskrit that abound in the early Saiva 
scriptures are much fewer in the latter, most of whose divergent readings 
are best explained as the result of rephrasing to remove such anomalies. 
In the citations that follow I have therefore privileged the readings of the 
Nepalese manuscript (N) as evidence of an earlier state of the Kashmirian 
text. 


Obviously a full collation of numerous non-Kashmirian manuscripts of the 
Svacchanda would be useful, but it is beyond the scope E pague Jic 
small test for chapter 7 performed by Nibedita ROUT using E TE To 
held in Pondicherry (IFP T.507, T.1032, RE 10832b, ES T time- 
351592), we discovered that a full collation would be volumin ik h ae 
consuming to produce and full of recent trivial copying p Grantha- 
that the text of the Svacchanda transmitted in manuscripts of the 


iL pn n attempt 
Script region is similar to the printed K aah eT को, b but that 
. १ way i rrectlo , 
has been made in both to polish away impe न ie adjustments as the 


Southern transmitters have not always made 


506 NiSvdsatattuasambite 
Kashmirians. More could and should be said on this subject, but the re 
lations between the Nepalese, Southern and Kashmirian versions ang the 
role of the Svacchandatantroddyota in the transmission of the Svacchanda 
are subjects that require further study and will therefore have to be treated 
another day by someone else. 

At the suggestion of Shaman HATLEY, who has discussed the sources 
and transmission of the Svacchanda at greater length (forthcoming), We 
therefore decided to give a text based just on the KSTS edition and on One 
old Nepalese palm-leaf manuscript, namely NAK MS 1-225 (NGMPP Reel 
No. B 28/18). The result is of course not a critical edition, but merely a 
collation the purpose of which is to point to an older state of text than is 
reflected in the KSTS edition. 

We have also not produced carefully considered editions of the fragments 
of the Nisvasakarika and Diksottara given below, but rather a collation of the 
readings that appear in the scant sources available to us. Where conjectural 
improvements have occurred to us, we have proposed them, but we have 
not combed repeatedly through these passages with a view to perfecting a 
plausible critical text. 


Finally, a reminder of the contents of the appendices and of why they have 
been included: 


Appendix I Svacchanda 7:285c-330b is parallel to Nayasütra 4:100-144b. 


Appendix II Svacchanda 11:316-319 is parallel to Nayasutra 2:6-9; 
Svacchanda 12:1c-82 is parallel to Nagasütra 2:21-102; 
Svacchanda 12:83-157 is parallel to Nayasutra 3:1-72; 
Svacchanda 12:163-165b is parallel to Nayasutra 4:12-14b. 


Appendix III. Nisuasakarika jňīnakāņda 42 appears to comment on Mila 
sutra 4:7.

अधर्मञ्च तथाज्ञानमवैराग्यमनैश्वरम्‌। 
बन्धते सप्तथा सा तु ज्ञानभावेन मोचयेत्‌॥ 12: 42॥ 


बुद्धिश्नाध्यवसायेन करोति विकरोति च। 
धर्मादीनां च अष्टानां लक्षणानि निबोध मे॥ 12:431 


उपवासं जपं मौनं अक्रोधस्तेयवर्जनम्‌। 
सत्यं शौचं च दानं च दया क्षान्तिश्च सर्वदा॥ 12:441 


विद्याभ्यासञ्च लज्जा च इन्द्रियाणां च निग्रहः। 
इष्टापूर्तं च तीर्थानि पितृणां चैव तर्पणम्‌॥ 12:45॥

धीगुणः प्रथमो ह्येष धर्म इत्यभिशब्दितः॥ 12:46॥

याचको दुःखदाता च भावद्चाधर्मचेष्टित:। 
नास्ति धर्मो न चाधर्मः स्वर्ग मोक्षं च को गतः॥ 12:59॥ 


अज्ञानभावमापन्नः सर्वं मिथ्येव भावयेत। 
नित्यं दुःखी परप्रेष्यो भारं यानं वहत्यपि॥ 12:601 


कृच्छुजीवी च सततमवैराग्ये न खिद्यते। 
राज्यं कृत्वा तु सामन्तः सामन्ताद्वामिको भवेत्‌॥ 12:611 


ग्रामाडृथ्स्तु लब्धेन वर्तते तु-म्‌-अनीश्वरः। 
न शोचति न चोहिग्नः पूर्वराज्येव क्रीडते॥ 12:62॥ 


अनैश्वर्यस्य भावोऽयमेवं ते समुदाहृतः। 
अव्यक्तं तृशुणं वक्ष्ये संसारस्य प्रवर्तकम्‌॥ 12:63॥ 


यतः सर्व्वजगोत्पत्तिः प्रकृतिस्तेन सोच्यते। 
तस्य धर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि रजःसत्त्वतमोत्कटम्‌॥ 12:64॥ 


प्रकाशभावः सत्त्वं च धर्मसत्वसमन्वितम्‌। 
संविभागी च सततं नित्यं स॒त्त्वोपचारकम्‌॥ 12:65॥

88 स्वशरीरोत्थितो dhada: सर्वदाहकः ] This half-verse has been printed in 
the KSTS edition as though it were part of a quotation of the Malinivijayottara, and 
it has therefore not been taken into account in the KSTS numeration. Misled by 
this error, Somdev Vasudeva has mistakenly included it, against his other sources, 95 
Malinivijayottara 13:21cd. Note that Ksemaraja refers back to it as belonging to the 


Svacchandatantra in his commentary on Svacchandatantra 12:90cd.

विशते चेप्सितां सिद्धिं जानाति च विचिन्तितम्‌। 
चैकारिके तथा रुद्रो ध्यातव्यः सिद्धिमिच्छता॥ 12: 98॥ 


ध्यानात्सिद्धिमवाप्रोति मुक्तो ऽहङ्कारबन्धनात्‌। 
ब्रह्माणं बुद्धिसंस्थं तु ध्यायेद्युक्तेन चेतसा॥ 12:991 


स्मरन्वै पूर्वबीजेन ज्ञानौघं संप्रवर्तते | 
दिव्या च जायते बुद्धिः संशयच्छेदकारिका॥ 12: 100॥ 


भूतं भव्यं भविष्यञ्च प्रत्यक्षं तस्य जायते। 
प्रकृतिः कृष्णवर्णा तु sper रक्ता विराजते॥ 12: 101॥ 


रक्तं च हृदयं तस्या बहुपादभुजानना। 
ध्यातव्या तत्त्वबीजेन यदीच्छेत्सिद्िमात्मनः॥ 12: 102॥

षट्मासाध्यानयोगेन दिव्यसृष्टिः प्रवर्तते॥ 12: 103॥ 


त्रैलोक्ये यत्प्रवतेंत प्रत्यक्षं तस्य जायते | 
एष ते प्राकृतो योग उक्तो मोक्षकर: परः॥ 12: 104॥ 


अतः परतरं पुरुषं मध्ये पद्चस्य संस्थितम्‌। 
चितिस्वरूपः पिण्डेषु देहमापूर्यं संस्थितः॥ 12: 105॥

निर्गतेन मृतो येन अचेताः शीर्यते पुरं॥ 12:1061 


बध्यते मुच्यते सो हि सुखडुःखानि वेत्त्यसौ। 
न तस्य वर्ण्ण रूपं वा प्रमाणं दृश्यते क्कचित्‌॥ 12: 1070 


न शक्यः कथितुं वापि सूक्ष्मञ्चानन्तविग्रहः। 
वालाग्रशतभागस्य शतधा कल्पितस्य च॥ 12: 108॥ 


तस्य सूक्ष्मतरो जीवः स चानन्त्याय कल्पते। 
आदित्यवर्ण्णरुक्माभमापबिद्वेव पुष्करे॥ 12:109॥ 


तारकेव हि पश्येत योगिनो दिव्यचक्षुषा। 
रागविद्याकलोपेतः कालबद्धञ्च रूपवान्‌॥ 12: 110॥ 


श्यामो वर्णेन विज्ञेया सितो जीवस्य देवता।

शुद्धस्फटिकसङ्काशं तन्दृष्ठा तु विमुच्यते | 

सिद्धिस्तु मानुषी लोके षट्मासेन प्रजायते॥ 12:140॥ 
बरैलोक्यदर्शने बुद्धिः प्रत्यक्षं तस्य जायते | 

क्रमते सर्वलोकानि ईश्वरेण समो भवेत्‌॥ 12:1411 


सोमादित्ये भवेन्नेत्रे चक्रे वै धीरथस्य तु। 
तन्मात्राणि हयास्तस्य मनः सारथि चोदितः॥ 12:1421 


अहंकारो भवेद्योधा गुणञ्चास्य महाधनुः | 
इन्द्रियाणि शरास्तस्य मृगो धर्मः प्रकीतितः॥ 12:143॥ 


यद्येवं क्रीडते योगी परमात्मा हृदि fen: i 
पुण्यपापैः प्रवर्तन्ते इच्छया परमेश्वरः॥ 12: 144॥ 


नाहं कर्तो न मे बन्धो सर्वञ्चेश्वरकारितम्‌। 
मत्वा चेश्वरविज्ञानं सर्वकर्माणि सन्यसेत्‌॥ 12:145॥ 


धर्माधर्मस्य कृत्वे प्रेरको हृदि संस्थितः। 
त्वमेव शरणापन्नो न मे बन्धो ऽस्ति Haas: Il 12: 146॥ 


सदाशिवोऽष्टभेदेन पूर्वबीजसमन्वितः।

गन्धैः पुष्पैः समभ्यर्च्य देवदेवेन संमतः। 
दीपयेत ततः पाशां हुंफडन्तक्रमेण तु॥ 9॥ 


एकैकमाहुतिं दत्त्वा पाशे पाशे न संशयः। 
प्रभाते विमले मन्त्री द्वितीये ऽहनि सुव्रते॥ 10॥ 


संहारक्रमयोगेन हुनेत्तत्त्वान्यथाक्रमम्‌। 
होमान्ते तु ततो मन्त्री पाशच्छेदन्तु कारयेत्‌॥ 11॥ 


हुंफडन्तशिवेनेव छित्वा तेनेव होमयेत्‌। 
हुत्वा पाशांस्ततो मन्त्री पूर्णाहुत्या तु पातयेत्‌॥ 12॥ 


पूर्णाहुतिक्रमेणैव सर्वतत्त्वान्‌ समुद्धरेत्‌। 
तत्स्थानात्सन्ततः पाशान्‌ तत्त्वं तत्त्वेन सन्धयेत्‌॥ 13॥ 


शुद्धतत्त्वं भवेद्धस्वमशुद्धं दीर्घसंयुतम्‌। 
विलीनमानं संचिन्त्य सन्धीत कारणान्वितम्‌॥ 14॥ 


एवं क्रमेण तान्‌ सर्वान्‌ हुनेत्सन्धेन सुव्रते। 
पृथिवीमादितः कृत्वा शिवतत्त्वमपश्चिमम्‌॥ 15॥

एष एव विधिः प्रोक्तः पाशानां छेदनं प्रति। 
तत्त्वानां सन्धनं चैव एष एव विधिः स्मृतः॥ 16॥ 
भुवनाध्वे कलाध्वे च तत्त्वाध्वे च वरानने। 
वर्णाध्वे च पदाध्वे च मन्त्राध्वे च तथैव च॥ 17॥ 


यः शिवः कल्पितस्तत्र तेन पाशानि छेदयेत्‌। 
भुवनाध्वे ततः कुर्यात्‌ कथयामि समासतः॥ 18॥ 


तत्त्वं संस्थापयेत्पूर्वं ततो भुवनजल्पनम्‌।

गन्धपुष्पैः समभ्यच्यै ताडनं च पशोस्ततः।

गायत्री तु भवेद्योनिः तया मन्त्रान्विशोधयेत्‌। 
सावित्र्या ताडनं कुर्यात्‌ ग्राह्यं तेनैव मन्त्रतः॥ 37॥ 


योजनं तेन कर्तव्यं तथा चैव वियोजनम्‌। 
उत्कर्षणं तु तेनैव सावित्र्या तु विचक्षणः॥ 38॥ 


पाशच्छेदं शिवेनैव कर्तव्य देशिकेन तु। 
पूर्णाहुतिः प्रदातव्या योजनाय परे शिवे॥ 39॥

THE NISVASATATTVASAMHITA 
THE EARLIEST SURVIVING SAIVA TANTRA 


Transmitted to us in a well-preserved 
ninth-century Nepalese manuscript, 
the Nifvasatattvasambita has come in 
recent years to be recognised as prob- 
ably the oldest surviving complete 
scripture of the Mantramarga. Al- 
though its historical importance has 
been hinted at by a range of scholars 
across the twentieth century, this is the 
first time its text appears in print. 


This volume presents a critical edition 
and annotated translation of the three 
earliest layers of the text: the Miila- 
sūtra, Uttarasutra and Nayasiitra. "The 
topics dealt with include cosmology, 
rituals of worship and initiation, and 
forms of yoga. A lengthy introduction 
sets these suras in context, in particu- 
lar by examining the evidence for 
dating them. There follow a summary 
of their contents, an account of the 
early manuscript and its three twenti- 
eth-century apographs, and a treat- 
ment of the various ways in which the 
language of the Nisvdsa deviates from 
Paninian norms.

Parvenue jusqu'à nous dans un manuscrit 
népalais du IX siècle remarquablement 
préservé, la Nisvasatattvasamhità est re- 
connue aujourd’hui comme ce qui est 
probablement le plus ancien texte révélé 
du Mantramarga conservé dans son inté- 
gralité. Bien que les chercheurs furent 
nombreux, tout au long du XX siècle, à 
mentionner l'importance historique de cet 
ouvrage, c'est la première fois quil est 


publié. 


Ce volume contient l'édition critique et la 
traduction anglaise annotée des trois 
strates les plus anciennes de l'ouvrage : le 
Muülasütra, /'Uttarasütra et le Naya- 
sutra. Les sujets abordés sont notamment 
la cosmologie, les rituels d’adoration et 
d'initiation, le yoga. Une longue intro- 
duction tente de situer ces sütra dans leur 
contexte, en examinant en particulier les 
témoignages susceptibles d'indiquer leur 
date. Suivent un résumé de leur contenu, 
une description du manuscrit ancien et de 
ses trois apographes du XX siècle, ainsi 
qu’un examen des écarts de la langue du 
Nisgvasa par rapport aux normes pani- 
néennes.
